extracted.intended_audience: readers of Vasari; art historians, students and practitioners interested in Renaissance painting, sculpture, and architecture
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative observations for assessing 14th-century Florentine painting, sculpture, and architecture as expressed in Vasari's Lives — covering composition, draughtsmanship, colour, technique, materials, narrative clarity, and artist conduct. Useful for art-historical assessment or practical guidance for makers in the Renaissance idiom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention and compositional plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Holding to almost the same plan in the invention, the manner, the scrolls, and the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency of an overall inventive plan and compositional scheme is valued; Orcagna 'held, nevertheless, to almost the same plan in the invention, the manner, the scrolls, and the rest,' implying coherence of design across projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portraits from life / likeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of 'portraits from life' to represent identifiable persons in paintings and frescoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placing real figures (friends, patrons, enemies) into sacred scenes is praised as an indication of observation from life and documentary value — e.g., Orcagna portraying Pope Clement VI and named contemporaries, Guardi identifiable by three red lilies on his bonnet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressive depiction of emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Vivid, believable rendering of emotional states in figures (sorrow, joy, jubilation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works are evaluated by how effectively they show feelings — e.g., the Judgment scene shows 'the sorrowful expressions of the damned' and 'the joy and the jubilation of the good' with vividness; emotional clarity contributes to the work's success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony and colouring
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of colour harmony and vivid colouring as central merits (phrases: 'harmony of colour', 'vividly', 'colouring is beautiful').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour handling — balance, harmony, and vividness — is repeatedly cited as a measure of excellence (Francesco Traini 'surpassed his master Andrea by a great measure in colouring, in harmony, and in invention').

rubrics_metrics.name: Draughtsmanship / drawing skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Precision and mastery in drawing ('drew very well', 'mastery in draughtsmanship').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fine draftsmanship underpins compositional clarity and figure realism; multiple examples point to drawings and preparatory work as evidence of artistic skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition, proportion, and grace
rubrics_metrics.description: Graceful arrangement of figures and correct proportion ('grace and proportion', 'composition of figures great and small').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-proportioned composition and harmonious grouping of large and small figures are praised (the marble shrine 'has so great grace and proportion' and its composition 'is very well executed').

rubrics_metrics.name: Architectural innovation and structural design
rubrics_metrics.description: Novel and laudable architectural choices that improve beauty and function (e.g., changing arch profiles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovations such as turning arches 'in half-circles in a new and laudable method' that 'gave much grace and beauty' are credited; design choices that improve aesthetics and utility are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sculptural technique and methods for joining materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical methods in sculpture and construction (e.g., 'built... without mortar, with clamps of copper fixed with lead').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention to construction technique and material-joining to preserve appearance and durability is praised; Orcagna's methods made the shrine appear 'shaped out of one single piece of marble.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze casting and finish
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of bronze work and polishing ('casting of the bands of bronze, diligently polished').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meticulous casting and finish on metal components that both bind the work and enhance beauty are identified as marks of high craftsmanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and success in relief sculpture
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling large-scale reliefs effectively (e.g., half-relief with figures of one braccio and a half).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful execution of reliefs at a human or larger-than-human scale is highlighted (twelve Apostles in half-relief gazing at the Madonna), showing command of relief modelling and spatial effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative clarity and symbolic storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear rendering of narrative scenes and symbolic relationships (stories of saints, allegorical arrangements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should be composed so that actions, hierarchies, and symbolic meanings read clearly (example: S. Thomas seated with philosophers and heretics underfoot; Christ sending down the Holy Spirit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifelikeness and animation of figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures that 'appear alive' and seem 'in the act' — convincing animation and presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A work is praised when figures give the impression of life (e.g., Madonnas and saints 'appear to be in the act' and 'she appears alive'), enhancing viewer engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional realism when depicting grief
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to portray extreme emotion (weeping) without destroying beauty ('although the lineaments of those that are weeping are distorted... neither spoils nor alters a certain beauty').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists are commended for rendering distorted features of grief convincingly while preserving overall beauty and compositional harmony, as in Giottino's Dead Christ panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of contemporary costume and local detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of period-accurate costumes, head-dresses, and civic emblems to enhance realism ('maidens who are wearing diverse costumes and head-dresses...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention to local dress and civic insignia gives narrative specificity and historical verisimilitude (examples: serjeant's bonnet with three red lilies; maidens' activities and dress).

rubrics_metrics.name: Versatility across media (multidisciplinary skill)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mastery and interchangeability of painting, sculpture, and architecture ('FECE ANDREA DI CIONE, SCULTORE; ... PITTORE; wishing that his painting should be known by his sculpture, and his sculpture by his painting').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists who excel in multiple media and let each inform the other are held in high regard; versatility demonstrates broad competence and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry, diligence, and professional conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Assiduous labour and moral character are part of artistic merit ('laboured therein with better design and more diligence', 'as pleasant, courteous, and lovable a man').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work ethic and personal conduct are treated as factors in an artist's standing; negligence or excessive commercialism (avarice) is criticised as impeding artistic development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modulation of tone for unity and subtlety
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting 'with unity and lowering the tones of the colours, reducing to their proper places the lights and shades' to reveal intellect and subtlety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subduing tones and carefully placing lights and shadows to achieve unified, subtle effects (Giottino's approach) is recommended for mature, refined results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrait placement and political/moral commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Using portraits and placement within scenes to praise or chastise contemporaries (placing friends in Paradise, enemies in Hell; painting Duke of Athens in contempt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition can function as civic or moral commentary; deliberate inclusion and placement of identifiable figures communicates political stance or personal judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and surpassing predecessors
rubrics_metrics.description: Surpassing one's master in 'colouring, in harmony, and in invention' is a standard of exceptional achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparison to predecessors and teachers is used to appraise artistic advancement; 'surpassed his master' signals noteworthy innovation and excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate material choice and structural prudence
rubrics_metrics.description: Select materials and structural forms appropriate to function and longevity (criticisms of unnecessarily heavy stone marzocchi vs lighter hollow gilded options).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choices that sacrifice practicality (excessive weight) may be censured even if visually grand; balance durability, cost, and structural soundness with aesthetic goals.
